name: hyp-54-half-split
comment: SPLIT COUNTERPART of hyp-54-half: every edge that is exactly TWICE another carries a flat 180-degree corner at its midpoint, so one tile's side may be met by two. The {5,4} edge 1.061275062 is exactly twice its half 0.530637531, and the tile carries TWO of those full edges, so both are split. The mirror segment 1.469351744 is not divisible and stays whole. Halving a regular tile always produces this ratio — the cut lands on a midpoint, and arc length is additive along a geodesic, in H^2 and on the sphere exactly as in the plane (AL, 2026-08-18). The unsplit board sees only the tilings where every edge is matched whole; this one is a SUPERSET of it, so containment is the check to run. Angles unchanged apart from the flats, which is why the curvature is too: a flat corner adds D/2 to the angle sum and 1 to n, and (n-2)*D/2 grows by exactly the same D/2, so the tile's area is untouched. HALF THE {5,4} PENTAGON — the hyperbolic twin of the dodecahedron board, and the second non-triangular half-tile. Four pentagons meet at every {5,4} vertex, so each corner is 90 degrees; a pentagon has no halving diagonal, so the cut is the MIRROR from a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite edge and the halves are 45-90-90-90 QUADRILATERALS. Scalene and chiral. Sides: the {5,4} edge 1.061275062, half of it 0.530637531, and the mirror segment 1.469351744 — the long edge exactly twice the short one once again. D=8 because 45 degrees is one unit of 2pi/8; the angles are [1,2,2,2] and sum to 7 against the 8 a FLAT quadrilateral would, so the deficit is 1 unit = 45 degrees = pi/4, the tile's area. The sides are DECLARED, not derived: a hyperbolic n-gon has 2n-3 degrees of freedom against n angles, so a triangle is pinned by its angles and a quadrilateral is not. They come from the standard regular-polygon relations, cosh(circumradius) = cot(pi/5)cot(pi/4) and cosh(side) = cosh^2 R - sinh^2 R cos(2pi/5), and the development is what checks them.
